gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much of the circle the four lenses actually close: Botslab's own angles for the G980H (170° front, 120° per side, 150° rear) add to 560°, which closes 360° with 200° of overlap when the side cameras face out, but leaves a 20° arc beside each front door (40° total) unseen outside the car when they are turned to the cabin.
standout_why: Compared against cartechtalk.com (lists the G980H's 170°/120°/150° angles but computes no combined coverage, no hours per card and no cost with a hardwire kit), gearjury.com (no prices, no fields of view, no storage figures), wikidashcam.org (blank price column, no field of view for any pick) and our own dealectric.com/best-4-channel-dash-cam (gives the 120° side figure and a 46 Mbps total for the REDTIGER F17 Plus, but no combined coverage figure). tomsguide.com came back as navigation only, so I could not compare against it. The derived arc is new against the four pages I read; it is not a 3 because Botslab does not say whether its angles are horizontal or diagonal, so the figure is a ceiling on the maker's numbers, not a measurement.
decides: It confirms the Botslab G980H 4-camera kit as the pick for a shopper who means front, rear and both sides, and it tells them how to set it up: side cameras facing out of the windows, since facing the cabin leaves 40° outside unseen, centred on the doors where parking dings land. It also answers ChatGPT's own closing question (sides or cabin): on this camera the same two side cameras do one or the other, not both. Parking recording costs extra on top of the camera, because Botslab's spec page lists the hardwire kit as not included; I could not read the kit's price today.

findings.label: Angle of view per camera (maker's figure)
findings.note: Spec row 'Angle of View: 170+120+120+150', orientation 'Front/Left/Right/Rear'. The page does not say whether these are horizontal or diagonal angles.

findings.label: Sum of the four lens angles against a full circle
findings.note: 170 + 120 + 120 + 150 = 560; 560 − 360 = 200. Derived by me from the maker's angles.

findings.label: Coverage with side cameras facing out of the side windows
findings.value: 0° unseen arc; 55° overlap front-to-side and 45° overlap side-to-rear on each side
findings.note: Measured from the nose: front sees 0–85° each side (170 ÷ 2), a side camera aimed at 90° sees 30–150° (90 ± 60), rear sees 105–180° (180 − 150 ÷ 2). 85 − 30 = 55; 150 − 105 = 45; 2 × (55 + 45) = 200. Treats the maker's angles as horizontal and ignores pillars and bodywork, so it is a best case.

findings.label: Coverage outside the car with side cameras turned to the cabin
findings.value: 320° seen, 40° unseen: a 20° arc on each side, 85° to 105° from the nose
findings.note: 170 + 150 = 320; 360 − 320 = 40; 40 ÷ 2 = 20 per side, between the front lens edge (85°) and the rear lens edge (105°). Same best-case assumptions as above.

findings.label: Hardwire kit and parking modes
findings.value: Hard Wire Kit: Not Included; Sentry Mode and 24/7 Parking Mode each marked 'Hard wire kit needed'
findings.note: So the camera price is not the parking-ready price. Time-lapse parking records at 1 fps; sentry mode saves a 1-minute clip on motion within 5 m; collision events keep 8 s before the trigger.

findings.label: Card in the box against the largest card supported
findings.value: 128 GB included; up to 512 GB supported, 4 times the included card
findings.note: 512 ÷ 128 = 4, so a 512 GB card holds 4 times the footage before the loop overwrites. The page gives no bitrate or hours figure.

findings.label: Power storage and stated temperature range
findings.note: Maker's claim; no battery mentioned on the page.

findings.label: Rival page's price and kit claim for the Amazon listing

findings.note: Cartechtalk's figure for an Amazon bundle, not read by me on Amazon. It conflicts with Botslab's own spec page ('Not Included'), so the shopper should check the bundle before buying.
